solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In speech, once again name a composer that's a concert performer

indicators.note: in speech tells us the words are to be said out loud, the spelling coming from the sound

parts.note: to cite is to name, so re-cite is to name once again, and the composer is Franz Liszt, giving re-cite Liszt

explanation.surface: A puzzle about naming a composer again, which sounds like a description of a concert performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In speech' signals that RE-CITE LISZT, said aloud, gives the entry; Liszt was a Hungarian pianist-composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A recitalist is a musician who gives solo recitals, so a concert performer fits as a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Others preserve a way of getting better still?

definitions.text: a way of getting better still?

parts.note: the rest means the others, the remaining ones
to cure meat or fish is to preserve it by salting or smoking

explanation.surface: Other people keeping something intact, wondering if that's a way to improve further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as 'even more', but it means motionless: this treatment involves lying still to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest cure is a treatment of prolonged bed rest, a method of recovering health while staying immobile.

clue.text: See 1
Complaint due to full implementation of some cutbacks

indicators.note: full implementation means the short form found must be written out in its complete expanded form

parts.note: part of the word cutbacks, its third and fourth letters, gives the medical short form T B

explanation.surface: Someone blames an illness on fully carrying out spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some cutbacks' finds TB inside 'cuTBacks'; 'full implementation of' says to spell out what that abbreviation stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness or disease, and this bacterial lung infection is a classic example of one.

clue.text: Outstanding examples of songs originally covered by Scottish singer

indicators.note: covered by places the opening letter beneath, i.e. after, the singer in this down entry

parts.note: Lulu is a Glasgow-born pop singer, famous for Shout

indicators.note: originally means the word songs supplies just its initial letter

explanation.surface: Great versions of songs first recorded as covers by a Scottish performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' reads as a cover version of a song, but here it means sitting under the singer's name in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A lulu is slang for a remarkable person or thing, a real humdinger, so lulus are outstanding examples.

clue.text: A Williams driver's entertaining set, primarily romantic pieces

parts.note: Serena Williams is one of the tennis-playing Williams sisters

indicators.note: primarily means the opening letters of the words driver's, entertaining and set are taken

explanation.surface: A tennis star's drive and entertaining set; the reader expects a Formula One Williams driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Williams driver' suggests the motor-racing team, but drive and set are tennis words.
explanation.definitionFit: Serenades are love songs performed for a sweetheart, hence pieces of romantic music.

clue.text: Far from rare words of praise

definitions.meaning: steak cooked thoroughly is the opposite of rare, underdone meat

explanation.definitionFit: Steak cooked through is the opposite of rare, and the same phrase is a congratulatory exclamation.

clue.text: Self-absorbed before playing one short concerto, say

indicators.note: before places the abbreviation ahead of the rearranged letters

parts.note: say gives eg, for example

indicators.note: playing suggests performing music, here working letters into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: short means the word concerto loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A self-centred musician launching into a concerto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the concerto; 'playing' then rearranges ICONCERT into OCENTRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone egocentric thinks only of themselves, so self-absorbed is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Officer briefly occupying belltowers …

indicators.note: briefly says the letters found are a short form, standing for a rank to be written out in full

parts.note: the letters L and T occupy the middle of belltowers

explanation.surface: An officer briefly stationed in church towers, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' finds LT in 'belLTowers'; 'briefly' marks it as an abbreviation, here expanded into the army rank it stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the army or navy, so an officer by definition.

clue.text: Those struggling to get a grip, having emptied rifles in pursuit of game

definitions.text: Those struggling to get a grip

indicators.note: in pursuit of means coming after, so the letters follow the game

parts.note: Scrabble is the word board game

indicators.note: emptied means the word rifles loses all its inner letters, leaving the ends

explanation.surface: Hunters scrambling for purchase after firing all their rifles while chasing game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests hunted animals beside 'rifles', but it is the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrabble is to scrape about with hands for a hold, so scrabblers are people fumbling for purchase.

clue.text: See 6
… which ring out around midnight, usually

indicators.note: around suggests moving letters about, so the words which ring out are rearranged

explanation.surface: The bells in the previous clue chiming out at about twelve at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring out' looks like what the bells do, but 'which ring out' is all anagram fodder, with 'around' its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The witching hour is the time when witches are said to be abroad, traditionally twelve o'clock at night.

clue.text: Now Wanderer's ear, nose and throat provide a sense of foreboding

parts.note: the present is the time now
Wanderer is the setter, so Wanderer's is I'm, I am
ENT is the medical abbreviation for ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: The setter's medical organs giving a premonition.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by pseudonym; 'Wanderer's' is the setter saying 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is an intuitive feeling that something, usually bad, is about to happen: a premonition.

clue.text: Comedian Billy at last acts the goat for radio?

parts.note: Billy Crystal is an American comedian and actor

indicators.note: at last means the final letters of acts, the and goat are taken

explanation.surface: A comedian finally playing the fool on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acts the goat' reads as clowning around, apt for a comedian, but only its last letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: A crystal set is an early, simple wireless receiver, an example of a radio, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Mentally disturbed people appear in film with this cast, oddly enough

parts.note: Psycho is the 1960 Hitchcock thriller

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of the words this and cast are picked

explanation.surface: Disturbed characters appearing in a film with an odd cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' looks like a comment on the cast, but it picks letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of THIS CAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychotics are people suffering from psychosis, a serious mental illness, so mentally disturbed people.

clue.text: Provided with the necessary shade around new course

indicators.note: around means the colour goes about the outside of the rearranged letters

parts.note: red is a shade, a colour

indicators.note: new tells us the word course is to be made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: A student given everything needed, with a coloured cover around a new course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns COURSE into OURCE, which 'around' sets inside RE...D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be resourced is to be supplied with funds, staff or materials needed: given what is required.

clue.text: Dish of cereal cooked with sugar or salt originally

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients changed by preparation, so the letters are reworked
originally means the opening letters of sugar, or and salt are used

explanation.surface: A recipe: cereal cooked with either sugar or salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives SOS from 'sugar or salt'; with CEREAL these nine letters are what 'cooked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a stew cooked slowly in the oven, or the pot it is cooked in: a dish either way.

clue.text: Make a dodgy manoeuvre as Conservative head of state (no parking involved)

indicators.note: no, read with involved, says a letter is to be excluded from the leader's name
involved closes the bracketed instruction, the parking letter not being involved

parts.note: Vladimir Putin is Russia's head of state
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A Conservative leader driving recklessly, with no parking in the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' tempts a generic leader; it is PUTIN, losing P as '(no parking involved)' asks.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut in is to pull sharply into the gap in front of another vehicle, a risky driving move.

clue.text: Perverted second-in-command, previously excellent

definitions.note: the definition is adjectival, the entry a noun for a twisted person, as in a perverted one

indicators.note: previously means the slang word comes earlier, before the extracted letter

parts.note: sick is slang for excellent, as in that's sick

indicators.note: second-in- means the second letter in the word command is taken

explanation.surface: A deputy who used to be excellent has turned twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second-in-command' reads as a deputy; split, it picks O, the second letter of 'command'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sicko is slang for a person with twisted or depraved tastes, someone deviant and warped.

clue.text: Suggestion for thriller film

definitions.meaning: Hitchcock's 1941 thriller starring Cary Grant and Joan Fontaine

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a faint trace, and is also the title of a classic Hitchcock thriller.

clue.text: Power source that might be found in any geometric form

indicators.note: form, as in giving the words a new shape, signals that any geometric is rearranged

explanation.surface: A power source hidden in some geometric shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'geometric form' reads as a shape, but 'form' is the anagram signal for ANY GEOMETRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear energy released by splitting or fusing atoms drives reactors, so it is a source of power.

clue.text: Exhibitions featuring former model? Interminably!

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: interminably means without an end, so the word for model loses its last letter

parts.note: to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: Shows that feature an ex-model, endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interminably' reads as 'endlessly long' but means the word for model is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Expos are large trade fairs or world fairs, a short form of expositions, hence exhibitions.

clue.text: Where you might find Dick and Bess, out of sorts after an exchange of letters

definitions.text: Where you might find Dick and Bess, out of sorts after an exchange of letters

parts.words: Where you might find Dick and Bess, out of sorts after an exchange of letters
parts.note: swap the D of Dick with the second S of Bess and you get a phrase for where poorly people lie

explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the D in DICK with an S in BESS gives the answer; it is not an anagram, just one exchange of two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are out of sorts, i.e. unwell, are found lying in hospital or bedroom beds for invalids.

clue.text: See 22
Extremely poor check for 3, perhaps

definitions.meaning: skint means broke, so the most skint is extremely poor
a check on the ... for the disease at 3 down

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one word, SKINTEST is the superlative of the British slang 'skint', meaning penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical test applied to the skin is used to detect tuberculosis, and skintest means poorest.

clue.text: Composer wrong about note? That's agreed, perhaps, after attempts to settle score

definitions.text: That's agreed, perhaps, after attempts to settle score

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the musical note
wrong suggests the letters of composer are in the wrong order and need rearranging

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A composer gets a note wrong; a deal is struck after trying to settle a score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' suggests music after 'Composer' and 'note', but it means a dispute; 'wrong' gives COMPROSE, which 'about' wraps round MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A compromise is a settlement in which each side concedes something, the outcome reached after negotiation.

clue.text: See 24
Important: pets might produce these (if you put them on your laptop)

definitions.text: Important: pets might produce these (if you put them on your laptop)

parts.note: key means important or crucial
to pet an animal is to stroke it, so pets are strokes

explanation.surface: A warning that cats walking on your laptop type things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pets' looks like animals, but it is a verb-turned-noun for caresses; whole, the clue pictures a cat on the keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Keystrokes are single presses of a key on a keyboard, which a pet walking over a laptop would make.
